summary: This work applies Pontryagin's Principle to determine time-optimal bang-bang pulse sequences for single-qubit $\pi/2$ gates, proving that the fastest implementation consists of discrete maximum-amplitude pulses alternating with idle periods. The framework is demonstrated on a transversally driven two-level system with exact analytic solutions, then extended to the fluxonium superconducting circuit where coherent suppression of leakage through interference conditions enables high-fidelity operation despite strong driving.
motivation: Low-frequency superconducting qubits offer long coherence times but suffer from impractically slow gate durations under resonant control. Standard approaches break the rotating-wave approximation at strong drives, necessitating fundamental limits on achievable gate speeds in the non-adiabatic regime.
method: Optimal control theory via Pontryagin's Principle constrains the control field $\phi(t)$ to bang-bang sequences: $\phi(t) \in \{\pm\phi_{\max}, 0\}$. For a TLS, analytic expressions are derived for minimum gate times as functions of $\phi/\Delta$. For fluxonium with parameters $E_C, E_L, E_J$, the optimization exploits selection rules in the phase operator to identify parameter regions where transitions to leakage states ($|0\rangle \leftrightarrow |3\rangle$, $|1\rangle \leftrightarrow |2\rangle$) destructively interfere, returning population to the computational subspace.
result: For the Heavy fluxonium regime ($\Delta/2\pi = 14$ MHz, $\alpha = 214$), bang-bang $Y/2$ gates achieve $1-F \approx 10^{-4}$ in $t_g \approx 19$ ns approaching the theoretical bound $\tau_L/4 \approx 17.5$ ns, with average Clifford time $\bar{t}_g = 50.7$ ns outperforming resonant control at 108 ns; the asymmetric $X/2$ protocol delivers $1-F = 10^{-5}$ in 1.9 ns, reducing average time to 33 ns. Open-system simulations including $1/f$ flux noise with $\sigma = 5.21 \times 10^{-6}\Phi_0$ and dielectric loss ($T_1, T_2 \sim 200$–$300$ µs) confirm robustness across Heavy, Mid, and Light regimes.
